description: The one error envelope every Dibbla platform surface returns. Its whole purpose is that a caller can tell five different failures apart without any of them leaking what the caller is not entitled to know.

fields.name: code
fields.summary: Stable machine code from the registry below. Never a free-text or generated string.

fields.name: message
fields.summary: Safe human message. Written for the caller, not copied from an upstream.

fields.name: retryable
fields.summary: Whether an identical retry can succeed. A caller must never have to infer this from the code.

fields.name: correlation_id
fields.summary: Opaque per-request ID for support. Carries no tenant information.

fields.name: field_violations
fields.summary: Per-field caller errors: field path plus a safe reason.

forbidden_in_message.summary: These never enter an error message, at any surface. Each one has leaked from some platform at some point; the list is the reason the envelope exists at all.
items: raw database or client process output (pg_dump/pg_restore/psql stdout or stderr)
internal hostnames, service names and cluster addresses
any token, secret value, or fragment of one
whether an object exists in another tenant

classes.summary: The request was malformed or asked for something impossible. Fixable by the caller.
The principal is known but not entitled. Never distinguishes 'absent' from 'not yours'.
The object does not exist within what this principal may see.
A dependency failed. The dependency is never named in the message.
The platform is not configured to serve this. Operator error, not caller error.

codes.summary: The request did not satisfy the schema. Populates field_violations.
A well-formed request for something this contract version does not offer.
A routine write was attempted without an idempotency key.
The key was reused with different parameters.
No credential was presented. Answered with a WWW-Authenticate challenge pointing at protected-resource metadata.
The credential failed issuer, audience, resource, client, expiry, not-before or signature validation. Deliberately one code: which check failed is not the caller's business.
The grant is valid but lacks the exact scope. Names the required scope, because that is what the user consents to next.
Role, entitlement or per-object authorization denied the action.
A destructive action was attempted without a bound, redeemed confirmation.
The confirmation was changed, expired, reused, concurrently redeemed, differently authorized or revoked.
The bound destructive plan exists but the same eligible human has not approved it.
The eligible human denied or revoked the bound destructive plan.
The principal binding, target, live generation/revision, normalized effects or digest differs from the reviewed plan.
The destructive plan's ten-minute approval window elapsed before redemption.
The confirmation was already consumed and this request cannot receive its bound terminal replay.
The approved destructive request is executing; retry reads its durable terminal result and never starts another side effect.
No such object within this principal's visibility. An object in another tenant is NOT_FOUND, never FORBIDDEN — the distinction would itself be a cross-tenant disclosure.
The object's current state does not permit this transition.
Too many requests. Retry after the indicated interval.
A dependency failed in a way that may not repeat.
A dependency is unreachable.
A dependency did not answer in time. A durable operation is returned instead wherever one exists.
This install has not been configured to serve the capability. Operator-facing, and never implies the caller lacks access.
An unclassified failure. Carries a correlation ID and nothing else.
